subject: OrchardApp integration: post-demo repro steps for auth failures and reranker timeouts
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Tim Koenig <tim@orchardapp.com>, Dana Lee <dana@orchardapp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: OrchardApp post-demo: quick repros, ask list, and next steps

Hi Tim / Dana —

Thanks again for the demo earlier today. Quick recap and the items we discussed that will help us reproduce the intermittent 5xxs you saw during the sandbox run:

- Concrete repro steps: sample request that triggered the 502 (you mentioned a batched reranker call with structured output). Please send the exact payload and headers (Auth, x-request-id, model).
- Token/audience: confirm whether you are swapping tokens between calls (service account vs user-level).
- Timeout settings and SDK version: which client are you using (npm package name + version) and what is the per-request timeout?
- Network path: are requests routed through an internal proxy? If so, can you share the proxy timeout?

We can take the logs you shared in the demo and run them through the same environment we used in the sandbox. Marissa will lead the repro work; Ben will scope routing and kernel-timeout hypotheses.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Tim/Dana: send the small reproducer payload + short log snippet (attach as plain text).
2) Marissa: attempt repro in isolated tenant with same model variant and pinning.
3) Ben: verify routing rules and typical failure modes (auth audience mismatch, KV cache churn during streaming).

Target: meet Friday (US) for quick sync after we have the repro.

Thanks,

Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.com
(415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood-postcall-sla.pdf (summary), orch-request-log-snippet.txt (please attach full logs when available)

From: Tim Koenig <tim@orchardapp.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Dana Lee <dana@orchardapp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 16:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OrchardApp post-demo: quick repros, ask list, and next steps

Thanks Rafael — attaching a tiny log extract and the request payload that failed in sandbox. Short notes:

- We saw a 502 at 2026-08-18T22:07:45Z. Attached line shows: "error":"upstream 502 - kernel timeout".
- Payload: we sent a JSON array of 18 items to /v1/embeddings?model=re-ranker-lite with a structured call in the same request (structured_output + tool_call).
- We are running redwood-js-client 1.4.2 via an internal proxy (proxy.company.local) that does request multiplexing. Proxy timeout is 10s.
- Tokens: the CI runner uses short-lived tokens minted for service accounts (audience: https://api.redwood.com/). However, our dev sandbox tokens are user-scoped with a different audience.

I pasted the two relevant snippets below and attached orchard-request-logsnip.txt.

[log] 2026-08-18T22:07:45Z ERROR request_id=abc123 upstream=redwood-main-01 code=502 msg="kernel timeout on attention kernel"
[request payload]
{
  "model": "re-ranker-lite",
  "inputs": [ /* 18 items omitted */ ],
  "structured_output": {"format":"json_schema","tools":["reranker","similarity_embed"]}
}

Let me know if you'd like us to toggle proxies or re-run with larger timeouts.

—Tim
VP Product | OrchardApp
--
Tim Koenig
tim@orchardapp.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tim Koenig <tim@orchardapp.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OrchardApp post-demo: quick repros, ask list, and next steps

Thanks Tim — the snippets are helpful. A few things I want to try in the isolated repro environment before we ask you to change anything:

1) Reproduce the exact request shape: a single batched reranker+structured_output call. I suspect the server is doing reranker->embedder fan-out which increases latency per token unexpectedly.
2) Pin the model variant to re-ranker-lite@2026-07-12 and set streaming off in the request to avoid partial KV cache flushes.
3) Increase server-side request timeout to 30s for the test run and monitor kernel wait/queue depth. If the 502 persists with extended timeout, we can assume kernel-level resource exhaustion.

Ben — can you check whether our runtime returns 502 for kernel timeout vs internal 5xx? If it's a kernel time window, we need to look at batch-size and attention kernel memory patterns for the listed model.

Tim — if you can also share the full x-request-id from the failing run (abc123 was the truncated id), that will let us pull the exact worker-level trace.

I'll schedule the repro today in a tenant that mirrors your sandbox. Rafael — I'll post a short playbook with the exact curl reproducer once I have the run results.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Tim Koenig <tim@orchardapp.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OrchardApp post-demo: quick repros, ask list, and next steps

Adding some engineering notes from the runtime side after an initial look at the snippet:

- Kernel timeout "attention kernel" failures usually indicate excessive sequence-length *or* an unexpected batch fan-out. In your payload the combination of 18 items + reranker->tools could create an internal 1:N expansion.
- Proxy timeouts (10s) + our default per-token kernel preemption can easily hit 502 if any single work item gets queued behind larger batches.
- Quick mitigations to try (in order):
  * Reduce batch count (split the 18 items into batches of 4–6)
  * Disable structured tool_call in the initial run and do reranker as separate call to confirm fan-out hypothesis
  * Pin model and disable streaming (Marissa suggested this)
  * Increase client and proxy timeouts to 30s while reproducing

If you prefer, we can open a temporary, instrumented endpoint limited to your tenant so you can hit it without the proxy path — that will isolate whether the proxy multiplexing is contributing. Let me know and I can spin that up for 48 hours.

Also attaching a tiny kernel metrics excerpt we captured from a prior repro (orchard-kernel-metrics.txt) — will post link in the Drive.

—Ben
Senior SRE | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:43:00 -07:00
Subject: OrchardApp next steps and Friday sync

Tim / Dana — quick update and confirmed next steps:

- Marissa reproduced the 502 locally when running the exact payload you shared with default timeouts; kernel queue depth peaked when the reranker did the internal fan-out.
- Ben confirmed the likely culprits and recommended the mitigations below.

Action items for OrchardApp:
- Option A (fastest): split batched calls into batches of <=6 and disable structured tool_call in the initial pass. Re-run and let us know results.
- Option B (deeper): grant us temporary access to a tenant-instrumented endpoint (48h) so we can run with increased timeouts and full tracing. If you choose this, please send the x-request-id from a failing run and confirm a maintenance window.

We'll prepare a short playbook today with exact curl examples and the SDK flags to change. Let's do a 30-minute sync Friday 10:30am PT to review findings — I sent a calendar invite.

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround on logs.

Rafael Mendes
